title: The Odyssey (2026) ★★★★★
text:
Third installment of Nolan’s Art of War:

There’s something unprecedented about every age. War is an ever evolving thing, and we’ll always have secret agents, physicists, and Bronze Age generals at the bleeding edge, bringing the world the next big thing. But with every next big thing is a decision to break a rule. A human principle to defy, a divine truth to deny. And there are a select few responsible with pulling that trigger.

Really similar to Isaacson’s Jobs biography in that it’s about the birth of a market, tech empire, and random guy at once. Every moment has to be significant to all layers of the story - in parallel. Really really hard to do, and he did it.

title: Mister Lonely (2007) ★★★★
text: All of his movies have this clearly very intentional quality, where every plot point, dialogue line, visual element, etc is chosen to elicit some specific but otherwise impossible-to-articulate feeling. I can’t tell you what the feelings are, I can only tell you about the movie. There’s nothing you don’t need, nothing to soften the sensation or distract from the abstract quality being distilled. It’s like inventing a universe to articulate an idea you can’t get across with words. You can’t be surreal unless you’re grounded in narrative. When the world is built from the ground up, it’s something different.

title: Lessons of Darkness (1992) ★★★★
text: Absurd. It’s all real, barely doctored footage, but it feels so absolutely foreign. I cant relate to the tastes and smells and touch sensations these people are feeling, let alone the emotions they feel. The movie doesn’t even try to set the viewer in the reality of the scene either - you WONT get it. It is a terrible flaming inky black goo flooding a city, without exaggeration. But the most they can convey is the apparent texture of charred earth and spraying oil. It’s alien and is treated as such.
